findings.detail: Cross-account integration tests are not evidenced by source inspection.
findings.action: Add two-account tests for notifications, ledger, recommendations, follows, profile and applications.

findings.detail: Self-demotion is blocked, but last-admin protection and full audit logging for admin user mutation are not established.
findings.action: Review and test last-admin invariants and audit trail.

findings.detail: Admin passes author role gate, but author novel collection remains filtered to admin's own owner ID.
findings.action: Document intended admin collection semantics and test.

findings.detail: Taxonomy submitter creator_id and creator_name are accepted from request body without a session requirement.
findings.action: Decide anonymous submission policy and prevent spoofable attribution.

findings.detail: Remaining API routes, CSRF/origin, DTO allowlists, private caching and runtime object isolation are not certified.
findings.action: Continue handler review and runtime integration tests.

findings.detail: Admin report status mutation has no audit(env,u,...) call in the reviewed handler, unlike several adjacent moderation/payment actions.
findings.action: Add an audit event with report id and status transition; verify this action is included in admin activity history.

findings.detail: Admin account PATCH does not visibly audit role, verification, or ban changes and does not establish last-admin protection.
findings.action: Add immutable before/after admin audit records and a last-active-admin invariant.

findings.detail: Donation approval uses a conditional status transition and linked ticket/ledger writes, but atomicity and failure recovery need integration tests against D1 batch semantics.
findings.action: Test duplicate approval, missing target user, and partial failure behavior using an isolated D1 test database.

findings.detail: Taxonomy proposals are intentionally accepted anonymously, but creator_id and creator_name are copied directly from the request body. This permits spoofed attribution and leaves anonymous submission abuse controls unproven.
findings.action: Keep public submissions if desired, but derive attribution only from a verified session and add per-IP rate limiting, moderation queue abuse controls, and spam tests.

findings.detail: Public vote listing includes requester username. This is public profile metadata exposure, but the intended disclosure policy is not documented in the handler.
findings.action: Confirm usernames are intentionally public on the vote board; keep email and private account fields excluded.

findings.detail: JSON responses default to Cache-Control no-store and HTML responses also use no-store, which is a strong privacy baseline. The sitemap is the explicit public-cache exception and filters to published, rights-eligible content. Cookie authentication uses SameSite=Lax, HttpOnly and Secure, but no explicit Origin/CSRF token check is visible in the reviewed request pipeline.
findings.action: Verify browser CSRF behavior with cross-site POST tests and review any future credentialed CORS changes; retain no-store on all account/admin responses.

findings.detail: The admin override on AI project routes allows an admin to run a project owned by another author, while ai_chapter_jobs.owner_user_id and ai_generation_runs.owner_user_id are populated with the acting admin's u.id. The project remains owned by the original author. This mixes project ownership and actor attribution in fields named owner_user_id.
findings.action: Decide whether admins may generate on behalf of creators. If yes, store project owner and actor/reviewer separately; otherwise remove the admin override from generation actions. Add tests for owner-visible job history and audit attribution.
